title: Mechanistic insights into domoic acid-induced cardiovascular endothelial injury: a combination of network toxicology, molecular docking and in vitro validation
content:
Abstract
Domoic acid (DA) is a potent marine toxin increasingly detected in seafood and aquatic environments worldwide, raising growing public health concerns due to widespread human exposure through contaminated seafood consumption. DA is tightly linked to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), yet its direct endothelial toxic effects and exact molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This work integrated network toxicology, molecular docking and cellular assays to uncover DA’s core toxic targets and pathways triggering cardiovascular injury. We identified 106 overlapping DA-CVD targets, screened seven hub genes (AR, ERBB2, GRB2, HDAC1, HDAC2, IGF1R, PPARG) via protein–protein interaction network analysis, and enrichment analyses revealed key roles of metabolism, inflammation and vascular injury pathways. Molecular docking confirmed stable high-affinity binding between DA and all core proteins. Gradient DA treatment on HUVECs dose-dependently suppressed cell viability, upregulated six hub genes while downregulating PPARG, boosted pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6 and raised Bax/Bcl-2 ratio to induce endothelial inflammation and apoptosis. In summary, DA drives cardiovascular toxicity and CVD development by disrupting these seven hub genes to elicit endothelial inflammatory response and apoptosis. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for DA cardiovascular risk assessment and suggest that monitoring these hub genes alongside mitigating DA exposure may inform preventive strategies against DA-associated cardiovascular diseases.
